title: Negative for M in the dividing fed vortices: vortices with an opposite-sign partner move no faster than others (median 0.020-0.025 vs 0.018-0.024 sqrt(area) per t on 3 seeds), and 3 of 18 dividing vortices travel 3 sqrt(area) between birth and division (1 in long axes); only in the sparse regime does a dipole partner double a vortex's speed
summary: dipmove.py (labkit's segmentation, tracker and lineage on the fed-vortex claim's packs; each track's sign from the rendered signed-vorticity channel) classifies every frame step by the nearest other body within 2.5 sqrt(own area): opposite sign (a dipole partner), same sign, or none, skipping area jumps. In the dividing regime (20261027T0712-c53-fed-vortex-claim/pack, seeds 0-2, ~30 vortices) median speeds are 0.020/0.024/0.025 (opposite), 0.021/0.023/0.022 (same) and 0.018/0.024/0.021 (none) sqrt(area) per t: motion is set by the crowd's flow, not by pairing. Dividing vortices (born by a persistent split, ending in one): 0 of 5, 1 of 7, 2 of 6 travel 3 sqrt(area); 0, 0, 1 in long axes; none of these spend most of their life in a dipole. In the sparse sighting regime (20261027T0602-c53-fed-vortex-sighting/pack_spots seed 1, 3 vortices) a vortex with an opposite-sign partner moves at 0.0088 against 0.0042 alone (same-sign close pairs orbit at 0.021), so dipoles do self-propel there, but slowly and with no division.

finding.operator: self-induced translation of +/- vortex pairs (dipoles) in a fed 2D fluid
finding.control: speed of the same vortices when their nearest neighbour is same-sign or absent (within-run comparison), and the sparse sighting regime
finding.result: dividing regime: median speed 0.020-0.025 with a dipole partner vs 0.021-0.023 same-sign vs 0.018-0.024 none; dividing vortices passing 3 sqrt(area) 3/18, 3 long axes 1/18; sparse regime: 0.0088 dipole vs 0.0042 alone

limits: Analysis of existing packs (3 t frames); partner status uses centroid distance, so a vortex touching a pair counts by its nearest body only. Only 18 tracks are born by a persistent split and end in one, because most daughters later fuse. The sparse regime is one seed with 3 vortices. A world where dipoles both divide and dominate (e.g. a lower vortex density with stronger gain) is untested.
